items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear overall (buildWindowSpec, resolvedSpec), but `window.map((w) => ...)` uses a single-letter name in compile logic. The new `.window()` methods also lack the JSDoc that sibling builder methods like orderBy have.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same `.window()` body, including name validation and the SelectionProxyHandler proxy, is copied five times. The WINDOW-chunk build is also repeated in each dialect. There is no shared assertValidWindowName, and window.ts sits in sql/expressions instead of sql/functions as the conventions ask.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked at the boundaries: empty and whitespace-only names throw, ntile/nthValue and preceding/following validate their numbers, and rows/range check boundary order. Numeric arguments are emitted with sql.raw rather than bound. All 130 hidden tests pass and nothing is silently swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is additive: an optional `window?: {name; spec}[]` field and the same `.window()` on all five dialects, with SQL unchanged when windows are unused. However, the helpers live in sql/expressions/window.ts instead of sql/functions as specified, and the method adds an extra callback-spec form.
